subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Census as Surveillance
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Census as Surveillance.

hook.text: A census counts people. But who gets counted — and how — can be a matter of life and death.

buildup.text: Governments have used censuses for taxation, military conscription, and tracking minority groups.

discovery.text: IBM's punch card machines helped the Nazis use census data to identify and locate Jewish families.

twist.text: The same data that funds schools and hospitals can be weaponized when the wrong government takes power.

climax.text: Census data is powerful. In good hands, it builds. In bad hands, it destroys.

punchline.text: Count the people. The question is who counts them.

quiz.question: How was census data misused during World War II?
options: It helped identify and locate Jewish families for persecution
It was used to rig elections
It was destroyed to prevent government tracking
